faq.q: Why put my hand on my belly?
faq.a: Your hand helps you feel the breath. When your belly moves out, you know you are breathing deep and slow.
asks: Tell me about Hand on belly

faq.a: A big muscle under your lungs pulls down when you breathe in deeply. That pushes your tummy out, like a balloon.

faq.q: When can I use belly breathing?
faq.a: Any time: when you feel worried, cross, before a test, or at bedtime. Nobody even needs to notice.
asks: Tell me about Three more times

faq.q: Why is the breath out longer?
faq.a: A long, slow breath out helps your body slow down and feel safer.
Stop and breathe the usual way for a bit. Go gently, not too big. Tell a grown-up you trust if it keeps happening.

facts: The diaphragm is a dome-shaped muscle under the lungs that helps you breathe.
Slow breathing with a longer breath out can help the body feel calmer.

quiz.say: In belly breathing, how do you breathe in?
quiz.why: Slow breaths in through the nose fill your belly balloon.

wrong.1: Fast breaths can make you feel more wobbly.
wrong.2: Holding your breath does not help you calm.

quiz.say: What happens to your belly when you breathe in deeply?
quiz.why: Your tummy puffs out like a balloon filling up.

wrong.1: It gets smaller when you breathe out.
wrong.2: Watch your hand. It moves out.
